newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila lines up 16,000 for Michael Jackson security.
newsitem.headline: Manila lines up 16,000 for Michael Jackson security.

text.p: Philippine officials said on Tuesday they guaranteed a security force of 16,000 to protect U.S. pop superstar Michael Jackson when he performs in this largely Roman Catholic country.

Jackson was scheduled to arrive on Thursday for concerts on December 8 and 10, both to be held in a private property owned by a Filipino-Chinese business tycoon in Paranaque town, just outside Manila.

Paranaque mayor Joey Marquez said he had formed a security force of more than 16,000 men to guard the concerts. The force included 15,000 civilian volunteers, 1,000 guards from private security firms and an undetermined number of policemen.
It was not clear how many people would attend the concerts.
"One thing is very sure for us, that we are going to put a strict implementation of security and peace and order," Marquez said.
Marquez spoke at a news conference held jointly with Manila mayor Alfredo Lim, who had opposed suggestions that the concerts be held in Manila's sprawling Rizal Park.
"We have nothing against the talent of Michael Jackson, but let us not cloud the issue. If it were not for that charge of molestation then I think everything would be all right," Lim said.

Jackson had been embroiled in a legal battle in the United States after allegations he sexually molested a young boy. Jackson vehemently denied the claims and prosecutors dropped their investigation in 1994 after the boy refused to cooperate.
Jackson agreed earlier that year to pay the boy a multi-million dollar settlement in return for dropping a civil lawsuit against him.
